items.stem: In a modular autonomous-driving stack, what is the usual role of the prediction component?

options.rationale: Prediction concerns road users' future motion, not graphics.

options.text: To estimate the likely future trajectories and intentions of other road users
options.rationale: Prediction forecasts how other agents will move so the planner can act safely.

options.text: To generate electricity for the motors
options.rationale: That is unrelated to the software stack.

options.text: To store map tiles on disk
options.rationale: Map storage is a mapping/localisation concern, not prediction.

items.explanation: Prediction forecasts how other agents will move so the planner can act safely.

items.stem: Why is a safety filter or guard often placed around a learning-based driving policy?

options.text: Because learned policies are always slower than classical ones
options.rationale: Speed is not the reason for a safety filter.

options.text: Because a learned policy can produce unsafe or out-of-distribution actions, and the filter enforces hard safety constraints
options.rationale: A safety filter constrains the learned output to provably safe actions, covering cases the policy was not trained on.

options.text: Because it increases the model's parameter count
options.rationale: A safety filter is about constraints, not model size.

options.text: Because it replaces the need for any perception
options.rationale: Perception is still required; the filter does not replace it.

items.explanation: A safety filter constrains the learned output to provably safe actions, covering cases the policy was not trained on.

items.stem: A validation team assesses an AI perception model before deployment. Select TWO practices that specifically improve confidence in rare, safety-critical situations.

options.text: Testing against curated and generated edge-case scenarios
options.rationale: Edge-case and scenario-based testing targets exactly the rare situations average metrics miss.

options.text: Estimating and monitoring model uncertainty on out-of-distribution inputs
options.rationale: Tracking uncertainty flags inputs the model is unsure about, which matters most in rare cases.

options.text: Reporting only the average accuracy on the training set
options.rationale: Training-set averages hide rare-case failures and overstate safety.

options.text: Removing all unusual samples from the test set
options.rationale: Discarding hard cases conceals precisely the risks that matter.

options.text: Deploying immediately after one successful demo drive
options.rationale: A single demo cannot establish safety across rare conditions.

items.explanation: Edge-case and scenario-based testing targets exactly the rare situations average metrics miss.
